effects.claim: Fixed-skill candidate runs C1 and C2 did not reach success: C1 never located the required cool bread, and C2 first located the CD source at step 46, leaving only one transfer before step limit. Under this skill and these two tasks, the different-candidate/open-closed search behavior was not sufficient to avoid step-limit failure.
limits: Joint attribution: the same fixed skill bundles search and transport rules, so this is not an isolated causal estimate of the search rule.
C1 never observed target visibility, so the stop-search-once-visible branch is untested for train:0021.
Only two tasks, one model, and one protocol; no generalization is established.

effects.claim: In candidate C2 (train:0034), after the CD source was eventually found, the actor moved one carried cd to drawer 1 and did not return it to the source, whereas parent P2 returned a later cd to the source dresser 1 at its final step.
limits: This is one non-successful episode; target completion and isolated contribution of the source-return rule are not established.
No post-transfer resumption for a second object was executed, so multi-object completion remains unknown.
The avoided source-return may reflect the episode's late source discovery and step budget rather than the source-return rule alone.

effects.claim: With only the last two pre-action observations, the no-retrace rule can permit revisiting a location that was uninformative more than two steps earlier; candidate C1 resumed fridge/cabinet cycles and candidate C2 resumed opened-empty drawer loops despite the rule.
limits: Specific refs demonstrate revisits; they do not prove every revisit violates the rule because the two-step window may not contain the earlier no-target observation for each action.
Limited to this fixed skill, history setting, and the observed C1/C2 runs.

effects.claim: In train:0034, under the fixed candidate skill with last-two-pre-action history, the successful sequence moved cd 1 to drawer 1, later collected cd 2, and moved it to drawer 1; no carried cd was moved back to its dresser source. In the matched parent run, the final action moved cd 2 back to the dresser and the task did not complete.
limits: Single paired task; candidate success is joint with prior exploration and cannot isolate u2/no-source-return as necessary or sufficient.
Not assessed on tasks requiring legitimate source-return or source-side state changes.

effects.claim: In train:0021, with only the last two pre-action observation/action pairs, the candidate search policy did not stop repeated visits to locations already seen without the target once those observations left the recent window; the candidate reached step_limit without observing a cool bread.
limits: Single task with target never observed in inspected locations; parent also failed and looped, so this is a failure to improve rather than a measured isolated regression.
Does not establish that the different-candidate rule is harmful where revisiting becomes necessary after a state change.

semantic_audit_notes: Direct finding f1 omits second fridge close at C1:35; actual close/reopen pairs are 3->12 and 35->41. Raw explanation preserved.
Direct C2:50 is look after first transfer, not resumed collection; insufficient remaining steps does not mean no post-transfer observation.
Conditioned source revisit was observed on one successful path; global necessity not demonstrated. Legitimate source-return requirement was not exercised, not proven absent from all tasks.
